data.hypothesis: Using direct B access for every size, with the parent's same 8x16 microkernel and disjoint OpenMP output tiles, removes panel allocation, copying, and packing barriers. At n=1024 this isolates those costs against the measured B-packed parent; direct access may instead lose if re-reading B across row tiles outweighs the packing cost.

memory_lessons.applicability: A direct-access candidate with the same tile and microkernel provides a matched comparison to the B-only packed parent, especially at n=1024.
memory_lessons.claim: The measured 8x16 AVX-512 parent with B-only packing was correct on all six tested cases and had repeated n=1024 timings of 0.0034113, 0.0034321, and 0.0034863 seconds (mean 0.0034432 seconds).
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Compare the controller's direct-access timings and correctness results to the packed parent before deciding whether packing or a different panel layout merits further testing.

data.notes: This is a direct-access ablation of the selected parent: the AVX-512 8x16 kernel, scalar fallback, and OpenMP tile ownership are retained; B-panel scratch allocation and packing are removed. The prior parent passed all six correctness cases and had n=1024 timings 0.0034112868, 0.0034320809, and 0.0034862971 seconds (mean 0.0034432216 seconds). The direct candidate has not yet been built, validated, or timed; no failed attempts or candidate timings are available in the supplied observations.
transformations: Removed B-panel allocation and packing; all sizes now use direct row-major B access.
Kept the parent's 8x16 AVX-512 FMA microkernel, runtime ISA check, scalar fallback, and generic row/column tails.
Assigned disjoint output tiles to an OpenMP team capped at eight threads; each tile starts from zero and fully overwrites its output.
